Which deterrence effects a design identifies

Source: R/dtr.R
dtrid.Rd

For the response y = b0 + b1 p + b2 s + b3 c to the certainty p, severity s and celerity (delay) c of the sanction regimes observed, a dimension that never varies has no identified coefficient, and the coefficients are identified exactly when the design (1, p, s, c) has full rank. Gives the rank and, for each dimension, whether its effect is identified given the others (full rank, or the rank falls without it). With log = TRUE the design is (1, log p, log s, c): the expected cost of an offence p s exp(-rho c) is linear on that scale, and with a response y the ratio of the celerity to the certainty coefficient, -b3 / b1, is the discount rate rho the response implies.

Usage

dtrid(p, s, c, y = NULL, log = FALSE, rho = NULL)

Arguments

p, s, c

The certainty, severity and delay of each regime: finite numbers, one per regime (p and s positive with log = TRUE).

y

NULL, or the response of each regime: finite numbers (the design must then have full rank).

log

TRUE for the log design, FALSE for the plain one.

rho

NULL, or a discount rate at which to give the expected cost of each regime: one finite number.

Value

A list: rank; ident and const, for certainty, severity and celerity, whether the effect is identified and whether the dimension is constant; coef, NULL or the least-squares coefficients; disc, NULL, or the implied discount rate (NA but for the log design); cost, NULL or p * s * exp(-rho * c).

References

Nagin, D. S. (2013). Deterrence in the twenty-first century. Crime and Justice, 42(1), 199-263. doi:10.1086/670398

Examples

# certainty varied at fixed severity and celerity
dtrid(p = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5), s = c(2, 2, 2), c = c(30, 30, 30))
#> $rank
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $ident
#> certainty  severity  celerity 
#>      TRUE     FALSE     FALSE 
#> 
#> $const
#> certainty  severity  celerity 
#>     FALSE      TRUE      TRUE 
#> 
#> $coef
#> NULL
#> 
#> $disc
#> NULL
#> 
#> $cost
#> NULL
#> 
set.seed(2)
p <- runif(40, 0.1, 0.9)
s <- runif(40, 1, 10)
c <- runif(40, 0, 12)
y <- 2 - 0.8 * log(p) - 0.8 * log(s) + 0.08 * c + rnorm(40, sd = 0.1)
dtrid(p, s, c, y, log = TRUE)$disc
#> [1] 0.09283505
